final_answer:
PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL - ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT
REDLINE ANALYSIS MEMORANDUM: Cumulus Systems SaaS Subscription Agreement
To: Margaret Yuen, General Counsel | Re: Cumulus markup returned Feb. 28, 2025 (Hartsfield Webb; J. Tull / R. Montoya)
Sources: template (Feb. 3, 2025), redline, executed Order Form/SOW OF-2025-0115-TG, Playbook v3.0 ("PB"), Kowalski email of Mar. 1. Merger-related context is deliberately omitted from this memo, which may be circulated to the business team; assignment is justified below solely as public-company M&A flexibility.

1. BOTTOM LINE
Do not sign on this paper. Counting the Playbook's own classifications, the markup has 17 Red items, so outside counsel (Clarendon & Finch) should be engaged (PB 1.4) and General Counsel plus CFO approval is required before any Red concession (TCV over $5M; PB 15.1). Four findings matter beyond the individual clauses:
(a) The redline is not a true redline of our template. Its "original" text differs from the template in many places that are not tracked (Section 3 below). Never "restore deleted text" from the redline; restore from the template.
(b) Cumulus is re-trading terms it already signed in the Order Form (99.9% SLA with chronic-failure termination, hard 3% escalator, 12-month connector warranty, mutual-agreement renewal).
(c) The deal already breaches the Board ceiling at our own price: the executed Order Form (3.5, App. B) totals $10,546,901 at the 3% cap, $46,901 over the $10.5M authority. PB 6.1 says only that it "approaches" the ceiling. Board re-approval (or price reduction) is needed even if every escalator point is won.
(d) The comments understate the markup. Several of the most aggressive edits carry no JT comment: the 75% termination fee, consequential-damages carve-outs, the indemnity swap, Provider termination for convenience, precedence reversal, auto-renewal, Texas law/venue.

2. DEADLINE AND AUTHORITY
PB 15.2 requires the written risk memo within five business days of receipt, i.e., by Friday March 7, 2025 (markup received Feb. 28). Kowalski's email assumes March 14; confirm an extension. 

3. UNTRACKED DIFFERENCES BETWEEN CUMULUS'S BASE TEXT AND OUR TEMPLATE (Red unless noted)
- Vendor violation-of-law indemnity (template 10.3; PB 3.3) is absent entirely. Red if deleted.
- Template 9.1(c) made IP indemnity, data-breach indemnity, confidentiality, gross negligence/fraud and Section 7 data breaches uncapped.
- Data: the "Customer Data" definition lost derived data/outputs (template Section 1); template 7.2 bars analytics, benchmarking and AI/ML training and is replaced; breach notice moved from 48 to 72 hours (PB 13: Yellow at 48); officer-certified deletion and backup-copy language.
- Warranties: template 6.2(c)-(g) (non-infringement, security, privacy, in-scope integrations) and the 6.4 "no AS IS" sentence are gone; fix period 30 to 60 days.
- Audit: template 11.3 remediation and 11.5 external-auditor (SOX) access missing.
- Termination: template 12.2(b) insolvency right and 12.6(e) 90-day transition assistance missing.
- Billing: template 3.6 (no suspension over good-faith disputes) and the "undisputed" interest limit are missing; the base adds suspension at 45 days overdue. Red-leaning for plant-floor ERP.
- Support: template 24/7 help desk and 30-minute S1 response replaced by business-hours support and 1-hour P1 (Order Form: Eastern Time; redline: Central).
- Exhibit C (DPA): sub-processor prior consent, TLS/MFA/pen-test minimums, breach-cost allocation (C.5), anonymized-data ban (C.6), audit extension (C.7), liability tie-in (C.9) all absent.
- Customer indemnity broadened beyond template 10.4. Yellow.
- Confidentiality: JT-04 claims to make it mutual, but template 13 already was. Missing: Customer Data as Confidential Information, five-year tail, trade-secret survival, equitable relief; "required by law" is drafted as an exclusion from the definition; 4.3 allows an archival copy. Yellow.
- IP: 8.1 claims improvements "whether or not developed in connection with this Agreement"; no assignment of Customer Customizations (template 8.2). Yellow.

4. PRIORITIZED ISSUES (tracked changes)
RED
R1 Liability cap (9.1; PB 2.1). Template: Provider 2x annual fee ($3.7M) with uncapped carve-outs. Cumulus: mutual 1x amounts "actually paid" in prior 12 months, no carve-outs; the paragraph also uses "paid or payable" inconsistently. "Paid" can be near zero before the first invoice is paid. Counter: template 9.1; floor 1.5x with super-caps (PB 2.1).
R2 Consequential damages (9.2; PB 2.2): all carve-outs struck (walk-away). Restore them.
R3 Data-breach indemnity (10.2; PB 3.2). One-way vendor indemnity replaced by mutual, capped indemnity. Cumulus disclosed an August 2023 incident affecting 12 customers. Kowalski proposes opening at 3x ($5.55M); I recommend opening at the template (uncapped), then 3x (PB preferred), with 2x ($3.7M, PB fallback, GC sign-off) as the floor. Put IP indemnity and violation of law in the super-cap too.
R4 IP indemnity (10.1; PB 3.1). Tracked exclusions are broader than template ("any third-party products" rather than solely-caused combinations; SOW integrations should not count as combinations) and a sole-remedy clause refunds only unused subscription fees. Red under PB 3.1. Counter: template 10.1 (refund plus implementation fees; combination carve-back).
R5 Fee escalator (3.2; PB 6.1). "Greater of 5% or CPI-U" is a floor of 5%, with no ceiling; PB names this structure Red. The Order Form 3.2 hard 3% cap controls. Math (subscription plus $725,000 implementation): 3% = $10,546,901; 5% = $10,947,418 ($447,418 over: a floor, not a CPI assumption as the Kowalski email suggests); 6% = $11,153,622; 8% = $11,578,212. Counter: 3% hard cap per the Order Form; fallback lesser of CPI-U and 3% (or CPI with 4% ceiling).
R6 Termination for convenience (12.3, 12.5; PB 5.1). Customer right deleted; replaced by 180 days' notice plus 75% of all remaining-term subscription fees, no refund. After Year 1 at 3% the fee is $5,978,926; at 5% it is $6,279,313; after Year 2 at 3%, $4,549,801. Over PB's 50% walk-away. New 12.5 gives Provider a termination for convenience on 12 months' notice (disguised as a terminology swap); a continuity risk for a VC-backed vendor. Counter: restore template 12.3; fallback termination after 24 months, or fee of 25% of the current annual period's remaining fees (e.g., $231,250 six months into Year 2); delete 12.5 or require 24 months' notice and transition help.
R7 SLA (5.2, 5.3, Exh. B; PB 4). 99.9% to 99.5%; third-party infrastructure outages excluded; maintenance excluded up to 8 hours/month; credits capped at 10%; credits "sole and exclusive" with chronic-failure termination deleted. In a 30-day month 99.5% plus 8 hours' maintenance allows availability near 98.4% with no credit. Maximum monthly credit falls from $23,125 to $15,417. Third-party infrastructure exclusion is a PB walk-away. Order Form 5.2 already fixes 99.9% and makes termination rights material. Counter: template; fallback 99.7%, 4 hours maintenance on 72 hours' notice, 10% credit cap only with termination under 98.0% over 3 months or 97.5% in a month.
R8 Aggregated Data (1.2, 7.5, JT-02/09; PB 7.3). Perpetual retention, no standard, no excluded categories, no use limit, and "not Customer Data". Red (valve designs, supplier pricing). Counter: delete; fallback NIST-based de-identification, no re-identification, excluding specifications, pricing and financial data, internal benchmarking only. Deletion also extended from 60 to 180 days.
R9 Data portability (7.4; PB 7.2). 90 days (PB walk-away over 60), "Provider's then-standard export format" (proprietary), $15,000 minimum for migration help (fallback cap $10,000). Counter: 30 days (fallback 45), open formats, free export, assistance capped at $10,000.
R10 Audit (11.2; PB 7.4). Paper review of SOC 2/ISO reports only; further audits at Customer cost with Provider consent. Red for SOX data. Restore template 11; fallback independent auditor, Thorngate-set scope, unredacted results, 60-day remediation.
R11 Insurance (14.1; PB 9). Cyber/E&O $10M to $3M; umbrella deleted; total falls to about $8M. Red (cyber under $5M). Counter: $10M; fallback $5M cyber plus $3M umbrella.
R12 Source code escrow (8.5; PB 8.2). Deleted outright. Answer to Kowalski: not a pure walk-away; PB makes it Yellow with a robust SaaS-continuity substitute, Red if deleted with nothing; JT-10 invites alternatives. Counter: technology escrow (documentation, APIs, schemas, deployment architecture), template release triggers, 90-day migration plan. Draft from the template (30-day deposit, quarterly updates), not the weaker text shown as deleted.
R13 Assignment/change of control (15.1, 15.2; PB 11). Mutual consent, Provider M&A carve-out, Customer M&A carve-out removed, our change-of-control termination right deleted. Red (no customer M&A carve-out). Frame as standard public-company M&A flexibility. The text also reaches transfers "by operation of law". Restore template 15.1-15.3 and 12.4; fallback mutual M&A carve-outs plus termination if the acquirer is a competitor or performance is impaired.
R14 Governing law/venue (16.1-16.3; PB 10). Texas law, Travis County/W.D. Tex., and Austin pre-suit mediation: both home-court elements, Red. Counter Ohio; fallback Delaware or neutral venue; mediation acceptable if neutral. Template jury waiver, fee-shifting and equitable relief (16.3-16.5) are absent from the base.
R15 Precedence and entire agreement (17.1, Exhibit A insert). Redline makes the Agreement control over the Order Form and adds a "supersedes all prior" clause, defeating Order Form 8.1 (Order Form prevails on commercial terms). Gap on our side: template 17.10 lets an Order Form override only a "specific, identified" provision, and Order Form 8.1 is general. Conform both so the Order Form controls on commercial terms.
R16 Integration warranty "AS IS" (6.3; PB 12.2). Red because Order Form 4.4 puts three connectors in scope: Salesforce CRM, ValveTrack MES (legacy MES) and the 3PL logistics platform, priced in the $725,000 fee with a 12-month warranty. (The Kowalski email names SAP and Kronos; the SOW names no such connectors. Correct before it goes to Cumulus or the business.) Counter: delete (A); keep beta carve-out.
R17 Auto-renewal (12.1; PB 5.2). Automatic 1-year renewals with 180-day notice (non-renewal notice due by Oct. 2, 2029), uncapped escalator; Order Form 2.2 says renewal is by mutual written agreement. Red (over 120 days). Counter: restore opt-in; fallback 90-day notice plus escalator cap.

YELLOW (Senior Counsel may take up to two; three or more need GC)
Y1 Warranty remedy (6.2): efforts-only, 60 days, exclusive. Restore 30 days and full refund plus implementation fees.
Y2 Fees non-refundable (3.1): preserve refunds on termination for cause, SLA, change of control, force majeure.
Y3 Force majeure (1.10, 13): pandemic Green (PB 14), but "cyber attack on third-party infrastructure" plus SLA exclusions (c)-(d) excuses hosting failures; delete or limit.
Y4 Feedback license (8.3): exclude Customer Data and Confidential Information.
Y5 Preamble "and its Affiliates" could make Affiliates parties; limit to use rights. Add the 50 read-only accounts (Order Form 1.2) omitted from 1.4.
Y7 Maintenance notice 48 hours versus PB 72. Y8 Service-bureau restriction (2.2); customer indemnity extension (10.3).

GREEN
G1 Provider/Vendor terminology. G2 6.1 no-conflict rep. G3 SOC 2 (Pinnacle, Dec. 15, 2024) and ISO 27001 recital, matching Order Form 6.2; make it a maintenance covenant. G4 60-day payment cure (favors Customer). G5 Publicity (17.9) with prior written approval. G7 Mediation, subject to R14. G8 Pandemic in force majeure.

5. COMPOUND RISK (PB 16, mandatory)
- Data breach (Example 1): cap R1, carve-outs R2 and indemnity R3 together limit a catastrophic breach recovery to about $1.85M with no consequential damages, against employee PII for roughly 2,200 employees, SOX financial data and valve designs, plus an incident history. Aggregated Data (R8) and weak audit (R10) increase exposure. Compound Red.
- Lock-in (Example 2): R6, R9, R17 and R5 leave no practical exit (75% fee, 90-day proprietary export, 180-day renewal trap, uncapped escalator) while Cumulus can leave on 12 months' notice without escrow (R12). Compound Red.
- SLA (Example 3): R7 as a whole (lower uptime, lower credits, no termination right) is aspirational. Compound Red.
- Precedence (R15) lets all of the above override the signed Order Form.

6. NEGOTIATION POSITION AND LEVERAGE
Open from the template, citing the Order Form as already agreed. Possible gives: restricted Aggregated Data, mediation, force majeure wording, publicity, 99.7% SLA, termination for convenience after 24 months. Do not trade: breach/cap/consequential structure, audit, Order Form precedence, Board-limit pricing.

7. NEXT STEPS
1) Demand a true comparison against the Feb. 3 template. 2) GC: engage Clarendon & Finch; authorize any Red concessions; memo date. 3) CFO/Board: $10,546,901 versus $10.5M. 4) Brief Finance on SOX audit rights. 5) Confirm the executed Order Form (our copy has blank signature lines; VP IT signed). 6) Counter-draft by March 17 for April 1 signing.

Note: based on the supplied documents; no external legal research was run. Texas/Ohio/Delaware points (penalty enforceability of the 75% fee, merger/anti-assignment treatment) need outside-counsel verification.
